newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 31.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
- North Korea agreed for the first time to talk with South Korea and the United States about the possibility of negotiating a formal end to the Korean war.

- The Clinton administration said doctors in California and Arizona who ordered their patients any drugs like marijuana that are illegal under federal law could lose prescription-writing privileges and even face criminal charges.

- The special American envoy to the Middle East shuttled between Israeli and Pelestinian leaders to seal an agreement for an Israeli withdrawal from most of the West Bank city of Hebron by year's end.
- A bomb ripped through an express train packed with holiday travelers in the eastern Indian state of Assam, killing dozens of travelers.

- China is preparing this week to carry out a series of legal reforms hailed by some as a step toward greater rule of law, but the pending changes seem to have provoked officials to speed up prosecution of political dissidents.
